Grace Curtis

Worlds worth getting lost in.

Grace Curtis is a science fiction and fantasy writer from Newcastle upon Tyne. Her novels move from a climate-ravaged Earth to a hotel travelling between worlds and into landscapes marked by ruined civilisations. She has written about video games and enjoys hiking and climbing.

Queer space western

Frontier

UK hardback · Published 9 March 2023

Follow a stranger across an Earth that feels like the edge of the map.

A climate-ravaged Earth, a dangerous journey and a love story that survives the crossing. Start here for a western’s momentum and the intimacy of a queer romance.

Check in for a mystery. Stay for the people who keep the place running.

Sapphic archaeological fantasy mystery

Heaven’s Graveyard

UK hardback · Published 18 June 2026

Dig for a legend and find a past that refuses to stay buried.

An archaeologist follows the traces of a figure others dismiss as myth. The discovery of a buried city brings old magic, political pressure and questions about whom history remembers.

The worlds beyond the page.

In a Hodderscape Q&A, Curtis describes how imagining people encountering the remains of Roman Britain helped shape Idolfire. She also recalls pitching its journey as a shift from the exploratory feel of Breath of the Wild towards the atmosphere of Dark Souls. That account offers a way into her approach to invented places.

Her games writing offers another point of entry. A Eurogamer piece about Blackwater Dam considers a real landscape as the setting for a game.
